title: Medieval Disputationes de obligationibus as Formal Dialogue Systems
dialogue_structure: Opponent/Respondent alternating moves from a positum; protocol-governed response and terminal consistency
commitment_state_support: partial: respondent state and consistency conditions
objection_reply_support: exact: opposition and constrained response transitions
legality_or_transition_support: exact: rule-governed legal moves and termination
response_quality_metrics: consistency/success conditions rather than learned quality
released_artifact: formalization and Dynamic Epistemic Logic semantics
limitations: not a corpus benchmark; one obligation theory; no modern released train/test set

title: Argumentation in Multi-Agent Systems: Context and Recent Developments
dialogue_structure: commencement, combination, commitment, and termination rules; proponent/opponent interaction
objection_reply_support: near: critical questions map to objections and alternative replies
legality_or_transition_support: exact at protocol level: permitted locutions and termination
response_quality_metrics: not a response-quality benchmark; protocol-level evaluation only
released_artifact: surveyed dialogue-game formalisms and implementation guidance
limitations: survey rather than one executable benchmark; heterogeneous protocols

title: ADEA: An Argumentative Dialogue Dataset on Ethical Issues Concerning Future A.I. Applications
dialogue_structure: multi-turn user/system ethical discussions linked to argument graphs
move_or_label_schema: argument-node labels plus misc; graph-grounded user utterance mapping
commitment_state_support: partial: graph nodes can act as state/commitment proxies
objection_reply_support: near: questions and argumentative user turns support objection/reply linking
legality_or_transition_support: near: graph membership gives constrained next-target candidates
response_quality_metrics: GPT-4 preliminary classification benchmark; label accuracy/F1 should be recomputed from release
released_artifact: 2800+ labeled user utterances; four topics; argument graphs; GitHub release
limitations: German only; preliminary benchmark; argument labels are not a full dialogue-game legality model

title: SAD: A Large-Scale Strategic Argumentative Dialogue Dataset
unit_of_evaluation: history-conditioned next-argument generation and strategy identification
dialogue_structure: 392,822 dialogue examples; 722,812 utterances; active reply chains across 20,619 topics
commitment_state_support: partial: stance and history provide evolving state but no explicit commitment store
objection_reply_support: exact for objection/reply and strategy transitions; reply chains are explicit
legality_or_transition_support: near: stance/history constrain candidate next moves but no hard legality oracle
released_artifact: training/validation/test split; released dataset and code should be paired with fixed split
fit_for_reuse: highest for transition statistics and response generation
limitations: strategy labels are rhetorical, not formal speech acts; no explicit attack/commitment/termination semantics

title: How to disagree well: Investigating the dispute tactics used on Wikipedia
dialogue_structure: 213 disagreements and 3,865 utterances with disagreement-resolution sequences
move_or_label_schema: multilabel dispute tactics including rebuttal hierarchy, question, clarification, and attack
commitment_state_support: partial: tactic history can be converted into commitment updates but commitments are not annotated
legality_or_transition_support: near: tactic ordering supplies a soft legality/quality prior rather than a hard oracle
response_quality_metrics: macro/micro classification F1; transformer label-powerset baseline
limitations: Wikipedia-specific; tactic labels do not encode proposition truth or full graph links

title: Exploiting Dialogue Acts and Context to Identify Argumentative Relations in Online Debates (ArguNet/Kialo)
dialogue_structure: contextual online debate turns with dialogue-act and discourse context features
move_or_label_schema: support/attack-style argumentative relations plus dialogue acts
commitment_state_support: partial: dialogue context enables state reconstruction but no commitment ledger
legality_or_transition_support: near: relation labels constrain legal target types but do not define all move legality
response_quality_metrics: state-of-the-art relation-classification results on Kialo; open-domain robustness
released_artifact: model and Kialo benchmark test set
fit_for_reuse: high for relation extraction preceding transition checking
limitations: relation inventory is coarser than rebuttal/undercut/qualification; not a generation benchmark

title: MAD: A Corpus of Multilingual Argumentative Deliberation
dialogue_structure: spontaneous NASA Survival Scenario deliberations with equivalent tasks across languages
move_or_label_schema: Inference Anchoring Theory relations plus dialogue acts
commitment_state_support: partial: IAT provides locution/commitment-like structure but no explicit commitment-store snapshots
objection_reply_support: near: dialogue acts and relations expose objection/support/reply transitions
legality_or_transition_support: near: act inventory supports constrained transition modeling but no formal legality oracle
response_quality_metrics: relation/act prediction and cross-lingual consistency analyses
released_artifact: manually annotated multilingual corpus with equivalent scenarios
limitations: small controlled deliberations; not an explicit game protocol; source language effects remain

title: Strategic Dialogue Assessment and the Crooked Path Dataset (CPD)
unit_of_evaluation: strategic move assessment and commitment effects
dialogue_structure: real courtroom cross-examinations modeled as adversarial sequential dialogue
move_or_label_schema: commitment-based taxonomy of discourse moves; credibility/Gricean proxies
commitment_state_support: exact: moves are defined as strategic commitment management
objection_reply_support: near: questioning and witness responses instantiate objection/answer pressure
legality_or_transition_support: near: sequential strategic effects support transition scoring but not a complete legal-move oracle
released_artifact: CPD annotations plus SDA evaluation framework
limitations: courtroom pragmatics is domain-specific; commitment effects are strategic proxies, not formal dialogue-game commitments

title: MuTual: A Dataset for Multi-Turn Dialogue Reasoning
language_or_scope: English translations of Chinese listening exams
dialogue_structure: 8,860 manually annotated dialogues; multi-turn context with one correct response among candidates
move_or_label_schema: response-choice labels and reasoning phenomena; no argument-specific move ontology
commitment_state_support: none explicit; latent conversational state only
objection_reply_support: partial: candidate responses include appropriate continuation but not typed objections
legality_or_transition_support: near: response selection tests contextual transition appropriateness
response_quality_metrics: accuracy against gold next response; human 94% versus reported best systems around 71%
fit_for_reuse: medium as a general legality/appropriateness control
limitations: not argumentative; no commitments, attacks, or explicit dialogue-game rules

title: MT-Bench-101: A Fine-Grained Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models in Multi-Turn Dialogues
unit_of_evaluation: turn-level ability evaluation and response quality
dialogue_structure: 1,388 multi-turn dialogues and 4,208 turns organized into 13 tasks and a three-tier ability taxonomy
move_or_label_schema: fine-grained turn/task abilities rather than argument moves
objection_reply_support: partial: can score whether a reply addresses prior context but not objection typing
legality_or_transition_support: near: turn-level context allocation and reasoning are useful response-quality gates
response_quality_metrics: task-level and turn-level benchmark scores with fine-grained taxonomy
released_artifact: annotated dialogue benchmark and evaluation protocol
limitations: general dialogue; no formal commitments, move legality, or argument relations

title: In Search of the Lost Arch in Dialogue: A Dependency Dialogue Acts Corpus for Multi-Party Dialogues
dialogue_structure: 33 dialogues and 9,000+ utterance units across classroom discussions, board games, and online game chat
move_or_label_schema: Dependency Dialogue Acts with fine-grained intents and structural links
commitment_state_support: partial: dependencies can support state reconstruction but are not commitment stores
objection_reply_support: near: linked acts expose reply-to/question-answer and other transitions
legality_or_transition_support: near: DDA parsing can provide structural admissibility features but no domain rules
response_quality_metrics: LLM/parser agreement and structured parsing evaluation
released_artifact: doubly annotated/adjudicated corpus with baseline parser evaluation
fit_for_reuse: medium-high for transition parsing and game-like interaction
limitations: small number of sessions; DDA intent inventory is broader than argumentation and not truth-oriented
